name: Björk
label: One Little Independent
lede: She cut an LP at eleven, howled for Crass at seventeen, made Iceland's biggest rock band at twenty, and has spent every album since refusing to make the last one again.

eras.title: Punk kid from Reykjavík
eras.text: An LP at eleven, then a run of teenage bands in a city small enough that everyone shared a rehearsal room. Tappi Tíkarrass and Kukl are where the voice gets loud.

years.h: An eleven-year-old gets a record deal off a radio broadcast
years.p: After a school recital of a Tina Charles cover was played on national radio, the label Fálkinn offered a contract and released her self-titled album in Iceland.
years.xp: Björk Guðmundsdóttir was born in Reykjavík on 21 November 1965 and had been studying classical piano and flute since about age six, according to Wikipedia. The radio station RÚV broadcast the recital nationally, which is how the label found her.

years.h: Tappi Tíkarrass: a punk-funk band named "Cork the Bitch's Ass"
years.p: Björk fronts the band after the original singer, [[Eyþór Arnalds|d405bc70-32de-4cab-8efe-efbddc9551a4]], is replaced. Bassist Jakob Smári Magnússon's father supplied the name.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band grew out of Jam-80, an earlier Björk project, and mixed punk with funk, rock and jazz at a time when Iceland's scene was built on very different sounds. The name, per the same page, came from a remark by Magnússon's father about how tightly the music fit together.

yt: Tappi Tíkarrass live in Reykjavík, 28 August 1982
years.h: Tappi Tíkarrass release the EP Bitið fast í vitið
years.p: The band's first record came out on the Spor label, with Björk as lead singer.

yt: Tappi Tíkarrass, "Hrollur", from Rokk í Reykjavík
years.h: Tappi Tíkarrass land in the film Rokk í Reykjavík
years.p: The 1982 documentary of Iceland's punk scene put the teenage Björk on a cinema screen and is still the record of that moment.

years.cap: Björk at La Seine Musicale, Paris, on 21 June 2022 during a Björk Orkestral show · Wikimedia
years.h: Kukl play their first show, opening for Crass
years.p: Björk leaves Tappi Tíkarrass for Kukl, a six-piece assembled by Ásmundur Jónsson of Gramm Records.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates Kukl's formation to August 1983, with Björk, [[Einar Örn Benediktsson|4c99c75d-e9a0-46c7-bb1f-7a9f65417914]] (trumpet, vocals), Einar Melax (keyboards), Birgir Mogensen (bass), [[Sigtryggur Baldursson|c7d8ab0c-292f-4651-9edf-2d79de385382]] (drums) and Guðlaugur Kristinn Óttarsson (guitar). The Crass link came through Einar Örn, who was studying at the Polytechnic of Central London.

Tappi Tíkarrass ended that July when she joined, per Wikipedia, though the band's album Miranda still came out on Gramm later in 1983. Björk's shrieks and howls become the thing critics write about.

years.h: Kukl's The Eye comes out on Crass Records
years.p: Penny Rimbaud of Crass produced the first album; the band also toured Europe and became the first Icelandic act at Roskilde.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Rimbaud as producer and Crass Records as the label. The Roskilde claim comes from Björk's own Wikipedia biography, which does not give a date beyond the 1983-84 period.

eras.title: The Sugarcubes
eras.text: Kukl's survivors start a label, a book press and a pop band. One single about a birthday makes Iceland's biggest rock band a joke the world is in on.

years.h: The Sugarcubes form around Smekkleysa ("Bad Taste")
years.p: [[Einar Örn Benediktsson|4c99c75d-e9a0-46c7-bb1f-7a9f65417914]] and [[Þór Eldon|1e4afef3-c22e-4776-8773-db4d13fa28ca]] start the art collective that becomes a label and a book publisher, and the band is built on top of it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page gives 8 June 1986 and lists Björk (vocals, keyboards), Einar Örn (vocals, trumpet), Þór Eldon (guitar), Bragi Ólafsson (bass) and Sigtryggur Baldursson (drums, from 1987). Their first single, "Einn mol'á mann", with the Icelandic "Ammæli" on it, came out on 21 November 1986, Björk's 21st birthday.

Björk's own page adds that she and Eldon married in 1986 and divorced in 1987, while both stayed in the band.

years.h: Kukl's last record, Holidays in Europe, comes out as they split
years.p: Björk, Einar Örn, Melax and Sigtryggur carry straight over into the Sugarcubes.

years.cap: Bjork performing at the Royal Albert Hall in 2016 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Birthday (The Sugarcubes song) · Wikipedia: The Sugarcubes
years.h: "Birthday" becomes single of the week in Melody Maker and NME
years.p: The English version on One Little Indian takes a Reykjavík art project to John Peel, who put it at No. 1 in his 1987 Festive Fifty.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says "Birthday" entered the UK singles chart at No. 65 and reached No. 2 on the UK indie chart. Ray Shulman and Derek Birkett produced it.

Sources disagree on when the One Little Independent and Elektra deals were signed: end of 1986 (Björk's page) or late 1987 (the band's page).

years.src: Wikipedia: Björk · Wikipedia: Birthday (The Sugarcubes song)
years.h: Life's Too Good sells past a million, per Wikipedia
years.p: The debut album is an unexpected international hit, and the band plays Saturday Night Live on 15 October 1988.
years.xp: On SNL, hosted by Matthew Broderick, they played "Birthday" and "Motorcrash". The follow-up, Here Today, Tomorrow Next Week!, arrived in 1989 to a poor reception and a long tour that ended with a hiatus, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Björk records a jazz album in Icelandic with a trio
years.p: Made with Tríó Guðmundar Ingólfssonar during the Sugarcubes break, it is a mix of standards and originals.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it her best-selling album in Iceland as of 2011. The same year she sang on 808 State's ex:el and met the harpist Corky Hale, whose session later landed on Debut.

years.h: Stick Around for Joy is the Sugarcubes' last album
years.p: Wikipedia describes it as a contractual obligation, better received than its predecessor.
years.xp: The band's final show was in Reykjavík. Wikipedia lists the breakup as December 1992, and the only reunion was a one-off Reykjavík concert on 17 November 2006, with profits going to Smekkleysa.

years.big: "The biggest rock band to emerge from Iceland"
years.h: The Sugarcubes end after three albums
years.p: That is Rolling Stone's verdict on the band, as quoted on Björk's Wikipedia page, and she was already recording in London.

eras.title: London and the dance floor
eras.text: Nellee Hooper, a house in London and a pile of collaborators. Björk stops being the Sugarcubes' singer and becomes a solo act with her own pop hits.

years.h: Debut sells about fifteen times what the label expected
years.p: One Little Indian guessed 40,000 copies worldwide; it passed 600,000 in three months.
years.xp:
Recorded in London from 1991 to early 1993 with producer [[Nellee Hooper|320dc49d-621b-4e46-8273-2e9d34bbfa01]], it came out on 5 July 1993 in the UK and 13 July in the US, per Wikipedia. NME put it at No. 1 on its 1993 albums list.

Björk's page gives June 1993 for the release; I used the album page's July date.

years.h: Post pulls in Tricky, Howie B and 808 State's Graham Massey
years.p: The second album was produced with Hooper, [[Tricky|5bf64d94-efd9-4334-96fd-e6197b0b02b8]], Massey and [[Howie B|522b0135-00dd-4307-adce-2bf7d51a253f]], and Spin later ranked it No. 7 of the 1990s.
years.xp: In the years around it she co-wrote "Bedtime Story" for [[Madonna|79239441-bfd5-4981-a70c-55c3f15c1287]], sang on two tracks for Tricky's Nearly God, and appeared on Plaid's "Lilith", according to Wikipedia. The press also built a "pixie" caricature around her that she has been shedding ever since.

years.h: A stalker incident moves the next album from London to Spain
years.p: Homogenic was planned for London but was recorded in Málaga after media disruption from a stalker incident involving Ricardo López.
years.xp: Wikipedia is the source for the relocation. I left out further details of the incident.

eras.title: Strings, swan, silence
eras.text: Three records with three different rooms: a Spanish studio, a film set and a world of microbeats. The widest fame she has had, and the most hushed music.

years.h: Homogenic fuses Icelandic string octet and beats
years.p: Mark Bell, Howie B, Guy Sigsworth and Markus Dravs produced; Eumir Deodato wrote the string parts.
years.xp:
Alexander McQueen designed the cover. It reached No. 4 in the UK and No. 28 in the US, and Pitchfork later rated it 10/10, calling it "one of the most perfectly formed records of any era", per Wikipedia.

Björk said the record was about Iceland's contradiction: nature everywhere and computers everywhere. Chris Cunningham's video for "All Is Full of Love" became a landmark in computer animation.

years.cap: Björk DJing off of her iBookBjork · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Dancer in the Dark · Wikipedia: Vespertine
years.h: Björk wins Best Actress at Cannes for Dancer in the Dark
years.p: Lars von Trier asked her to score his film, then talked her into the lead role of Selma. The film took the Palme d'Or.
years.xp:
She has said she never wanted to act and only made an exception for von Trier. The soundtrack Selmasongs came out on 18 September 2000, and "I've Seen It All" (a duet with [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]]) was nominated for the Best Original Song Oscar, losing to Bob Dylan.

At the March 2001 ceremony she wore the swan dress that also appeared on the cover of her next album, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Vespertine: microbeats and harps, at whisper volume
years.p: Matmos, Zeena Parkins and Thomas Knak supplied the small sounds, and she toured it in opera houses.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.2; Metacritic averages 88 from 28 reviews, per Wikipedia. The 2001 tour brought an Inuit women's choir recruited in Greenland, including a night at the Royal Opera House in London on 16 December. MTV banned the videos for "Pagan Poetry" and "Cocoon" for sexual content.

eras.title: Voices and a flag
eras.text: A record made almost entirely of voices, a dress that opens into a map, and the first US top ten. She also plays one last Sugarcubes night.

years.h: Medúlla is nearly all human voice
years.p: Tanya Tagaq, Rahzel, Mike Patton and Robert Wyatt join choirs, and it debuts at No. 14 on the US chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the record uses voices plus basic electronic programming and occasional instruments. One track sets E.E. Cummings.

years.h: Björk sings "Oceania" at the Athens Olympics
years.p: Her dress unfurled across the stadium into a 10,000 square foot map of the world.
years.xp: The song was written for the occasion, with beatboxer Shlomo and a London choir. A version with Kelis circulated online and ended up as a B-side to "Who Is It".

years.h: The Sugarcubes reunite for one night in Reykjavík
years.p: A 20th-anniversary concert, with profits donated to Smekkleysa.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band confirmed it had no plans for further shows or recording.

years.h: Volta takes Timbaland, Antony and a brass band to No. 9
years.p: It is her first US top ten, and the tour uses the Reactable, a touch-table instrument.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it sold 43,000 copies in its first US week. Guests included Toumani Diabaté, Konono No. 1 and [[Antony Hegarty|91b67275-db2c-4fc2-b51f-82978aeb5c41]]; the tour ran about 18 months and returned to Latin America after nine years.

eras.title: Apps, a breakup, a leak
eras.text: Science, software and a museum show, then the most personal record she has made. The leak is the plot twist.

years.h: Biophilia ships as an iPad app, one per song
years.p: First shown at Manchester International Festival on 30 June 2011, with a gameleste built for the record.
years.xp: The apps were later inducted into the Museum of Modern Art's permanent collection, per Wikipedia, the first apps to be. She also ran science workshops for Reykjavík schoolchildren.

years.h: Vulnicura leaks two months early; Björk releases it on the 20th
years.p: Björk on making the album with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and the Haxan Cloak, a record about her breakup with Matthew Barney.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the label moved the release up to 20 January, and Pitchfork awarded it 8.6. Metacritic has it at 87 across 40 reviews.

years.cap: Björk and the legendary "Swan Dress" designed by Marjan Pejoski (here at 2001 Academy… · Wikimedia
years.h: MoMA opens a Björk retrospective with a room of 49 hidden speakers
years.p: It ran through 7 June 2015, pairing instruments built for Biophilia with a video installation for "Black Lake".
years.xp: The show included a Songlines section of notebooks, costumes and props. A book, Björk: Archives, followed.

years.h: Utopia is her second album with Arca
years.p: It has been described as a "Tinder album" about searching for love and a utopia, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: It was nominated for a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. The 2019 staged show Cornucopia opened at The Shed in New York's Hudson Yards.

eras.title: Back down to earth
eras.text: After her mother died in 2018 she made a record about what lives under the ground, and then kept collaborating at the edges.

years.h: Björk and Sjón co-write The Northman, and her daughter makes her film debut
years.p: Robert Eggers' film, in which Björk appears, reached US cinemas on 22 April 2022.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fossora · Album of the Year: Fossora · Metacritic: Fossora
years.h: Fossora: clarinets, gabber and a mushroom
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and ranked it No. 12 of 2022; Metacritic has it at 85 from 22 reviews.
years.xp:
It is the first album she produced entirely herself, recorded in Iceland in 2021-22. The record is partly a grief album for her mother, Hildur Rúna Hauksdóttir: "Sorrowful Soil" is a eulogy and "Ancestress" an epitaph, per Wikipedia.

Collaborators include the clarinet sextet Murmuri, serpentwithfeet and the Indonesian duo Gabber Modus Operandi. She described mushrooms as underground, "psychedelic" things that "pop up everywhere". It reached No. 11 in the UK and earned a Grammy nomination.

years.h: "Oral" with Rosalía supports Seyðisfjörður against fish farming
years.p: Sega Bodega produced the single; proceeds went to Aegis, the group Björk co-founded, which opposes Norwegian fish farming in the fjord.
years.xp: Rosalía returned the favor on "Berghain" in 2025, per Wikipedia.
